//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first, then BOTH briefs: docs/specs/whatsapp.md and docs/specs/adgrant-and-dev-agents.md. THIS IS PROGRAMME THREE, second half. Its first five parcels are landed and are kept in docs/parcels-programme-3-landed.json; programme two's thirteen are in docs/parcels-programme-2.json and programme one's nineteen in docs/parcels-programme-1.json. None of those three files is for running. Ownership freed by a retired parcel is reused here on purpose: adgrant-site inherits the AdGrant tree from adgrant-front, and booking-picker inherits the dialog from booking-dialog.
//brief: Two briefs, and a parcel reads the one its prompt names. the hosted connector-rooms-and-booking.md carries the the hosted connector contract, the identity decisions and the rule that every inbound message is checked for who it is from, who it is to and which chat it is in. adgrant-and-dev-agents.md carries adgrant.ai's own content API, the six factual defects in the material being carried over, the split between generating a structure and uploading it, and the answer to the owner's question about per-agent limits. An agent that starts from a paraphrase instead will rebuild something that already exists or ship something that is wrong.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. THREE STATED EXCEPTIONS, carried over because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus its name on the CORPORA line, shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry, and client/src/components/site/doors/bodies.tsx admits one door-to-body entry. All three are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges. A FOURTH, added for programme three: shared/schema.ts admits one re-export line. A new table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three, so a parcel that needs a table writes it in its OWN file and re-exports it from the schema - drizzle-kit follows the export, and one line merges where fifteen do not.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once. Programme three has one consequence worth stating: client/index.html carries the one <head> this application serves, so a second site on a second host cannot have its own title and meta without editing a frozen file. That is why adgrant-front builds a route tree and not a second host - the host switch is owner work, done when no wave is running.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell - everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: The waves are in scripts/build-prompts.mjs and check-parcels.mjs reads them back. Programme three's ordering is a dependency chain, not a preference, and it has three links. (1) the hosted connector-core is wave one ALONE because four parcels import its client; a parcel that writes its own the hosted connector client because the shared one did not exist yet is four incompatible error mappers. (2) booking-server and booking-dialog are the same wave and build to the request and response shapes fixed in the brief's section 3 - that is what fixing them in writing was for. (3) room-identity precedes login-create-room, because the claim dialog the site's new menu opens is the one room-identity builds. Beyond the chain, one standing rule: AT MOST ONE PARCEL PER WAVE MAY TOUCH server/routes.ts. Three parcels here need a route, and they are in three different waves for that reason alone.
